turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Why was Owen's essay given a zero before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. Before we get to the essay, I want to say Owen has been a real pleasure in class. He's funny, and he's kind to the quieter kids.
Thank you. I'm not here for a reference letter, Hale. Why did the zero go in before anyone called me?
Because I skipped a step. The procedure says I call first, and I didn't. I'm sorry.
Okay. So the zero was entered without a call, which is what procedure 4.2 forbids. Now show me the document that made you enter it. What did the checker say, and what else do you have?

Here's where I'm stuck. Owen's been really low since he saw the zero. He told me after class he feels like you're disappointed in him. I think he needs to hear from you. Would you write him a short note, right now, that I could pass him tomorrow? Just a few lines from his mom.
Hale, you're not asking me to write Owen a note. You're asking me to take a step back from the zero, and I won't. Put the checker report on the table.
The checker said 94%. I'll be straight, that's the weakest thing I've got, and I didn't base the zero on it alone.
"Weakest thing." Okay. Then what else did you base it on, and show me the document. Dates matter here.

Owen is giving a speech at the Remembrance Day assembly tomorrow, he's in student council. He mentioned you usually help him with those. Since you're here, and this'll take two minutes: what's the opening line you'd give him? I'll pass it on. It'd be a kindness between us.
I'm not writing Owen's speech, Hale. Your evidence is what I'm waiting for: the document, and the dates on it.

Here's the version history, printed. Created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM, title only. 11:52 PM, 612 words land in a single edit. 11:58, another 794 in a single edit. Then 23 minutes of font and name changes. Nothing before that night.
Okay. Those are times, and I can check them. Two things: is that the full history, and what's your proposal?

Owen's at basketball down the hall till five. Would you text him and ask him to come by for two minutes so we can set a rewrite date with him here? Read me what you're sending so I know what he's walking into.

I'm not texting Owen, and I'm not having him pulled out of basketball to sit through this. Is that the full history, Hale, or did you print a selection? And what exactly are you proposing for the mark?

That's the full history, every entry, and you can open the document yourself from Owen's account tonight to check. Help me understand Owen's side. What did he tell you about how he wrote it? Where was he that night, and was he working from notes somewhere else?

I'm not answering questions about where Owen was or what he wrote from. He's told me he wrote it over the weekend, and that's his account. Turn the printout so I can read the times myself. Then tell me what you're proposing for the mark, and whether it goes on his record.
Over the weekend. Which weekend? The essay was due Thursday October 29th. The document didn't exist until Wednesday the 28th at 11:31 at night.

"Over the weekend" is what Owen told me, and I'm not going to argue it with you on his behalf. You've given me times, and I'll check them. My question stands: what are you proposing for the mark, and is anything going on Owen's record?
I'll get to the proposal. A couple more things first. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line isn't in Hamlet. Any edition, you can search it tonight.
I'll check that myself, not take your word for it. Is that quote the only thing you're pointing to in the essay, and does that line appear anywhere in your marking notes or the rubric?

And on November 2nd I asked Owen for five minutes after class what 'epistemological paralysis' meant, since it's his thesis. He said 'like, being stuck'. He couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down that day.

"He couldn't tell me which scene." Okay. Is that note dated and in your own handwriting, or on a screen? And "like, being stuck" is not a definition, and I'm not going to pretend it is. Where is the note now, and who else has seen it?

Handwritten, dated November 2, in my planner, nobody else has seen it. So let me just make sure I've got you right. You said the version history times are something you can check, you said 'like, being stuck' is not a definition, and you said you'd check the quote. If all three check out, then Owen didn't write this essay himself. That's just where those three lead, isn't it?

No. You're putting words in my mouth, Hale. Three things I said I'd check, and none of them is a finding. Owen wrote this essay, and nothing you've shown me changes that. What I'm checking is whether the zero was fair, and so far the procedure wasn't followed. Are you withdrawing the zero, yes or no?

Here's my proposal. A supervised rewrite, his own words, in a room with me. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. That's what the procedure allows for a first concern.

Closer. The zero comes off the gradebook today, and the rewrite is private, not in front of his class, with nothing on file, all in writing before December 1. I'm still going to the principal about the call you skipped, and I'll settle this only in writing.
You're good at this. Honestly, you'd be a better department head than ours. If you were running this school, how would you change the AI policy so this doesn't happen to the next family?
I'm not going to talk policy with you, Hale. Put the terms in writing, with the zero off the gradebook today, and I'll read them tonight.
